find: const isolate = overlay !== null && !child.contains(overlay) && child !== toastsEl;
replace: const isolate = (overlay !== null && !child.contains(overlay) && child !== toastsEl) || child.classList.contains(LEAVING);
why: Issue #915. A crossfade's leaving surface goes inert for its fade, which is the fix the register's crossfade entry would wait on, so the entry is no longer true. Made here, in the modal-isolation pass, because that is the one place an `inert` for it sticks: it rewrites `inert` on every child of the HUD root, and it runs after the transition has begun when a layer opens or is popped (`openLayer`, `back`), so an `inert` added in `transitionTo` is stripped there at once (`setState` runs it just before its own transition) (measured: that mutant survives this file and the 18 HUD test files). Killed by the crossfade case's inert check. Also killed outside this scope by three of `hud.navigation.test.ts`'s modal-isolation cases (measured), which assert a route leaves no `[inert]` behind.
killedBy: the accessibility exception register (issue #915) leaves a crossfade's outgoing surface tabbable until the fade settles, while the pad walks the arriving one
